llm.summary: The skill appears to implement an Upbit auto-trader as claimed, but it ships with committed Upbit API keys in config.json and inconsistently declares no credentials required — this mismatch and the presence of hard-coded keys are a serious concern.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (Upbit auto-trader) align with the code and required binary (node). The code implements monitoring, event processing, order execution, and Upbit API client logic consistent with the stated purpose. Minor inconsistency: SKILL.md declares no required env vars and emphasizes Cron/exec runs, while the implementation expects a local config.json with API keys (see environment proportionality).
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions (SKILL.md and skill.js entrypoint) are narrowly scoped: read ./config.json, run one of the node commands, and update resource files under resources/. The skill does not instruct reading unrelated system files or sending data to unknown external endpoints in the provided docs. The runtime behavior described (writing events/positions/heartbeat files and producing a SUMMARY line) matches the code.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec; the skill is shipped as source and expects Node/npm. Dependencies (axios, jsonwebtoken, uuid) are common and consistent with a client that talks to an API and signs requests. No remote downloads or obscure install steps are present.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: High concern: the repository includes a committed config.json containing an Upbit accessKey and secretKey. SKILL.md explicitly warns 'do NOT commit config.json' yet the published package includes it. The skill declares no required environment variables (none listed) and no primary credential, but the runtime reads API credentials from config.json — a mismatch. Shipping hard-coded API keys in the package is disproportionate and dangerous (credential exposure / potential misuse).
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request elevated platform privileges or 'always: true'. It writes/maintains its own resources/locks within its project directory (resources/), which is consistent with its function and appropriate for cron jobs.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Do NOT run this skill as-is. It ships with committed Upbit credentials in config.json (these keys may be active and could allow trading or withdrawals). Before using the skill: 1) remove the bundled config.json and any hard-coded keys, or replace them with your own keys created for this purpose; 2) if you (or the platform) already used the included keys, rotate/revoke those Upbit API keys immediately; 3) run the skill in dry-run mode (set execution.dryRun=true) and test with smoke_test to observe behavior without placing orders; 4) review scripts/execution/upbitClient.js to confirm it calls only Upbit endpoints and does not send sensitive data to other hosts; 5) run the skill in an isolated environment with limited network access until you audit it; 6) prefer storing credentials in a secure secret store or environment variables and never commit them to source control. The code otherwise matches its trading purpose, but the hard-coded/committed credentials make this package unsafe to run without remediation.
llm.findings: [HARD_CODED_SECRETS] unexpected: config.json appears in the package and contains upbit.accessKey and upbit.secretKey values. A trading skill needs API credentials, but they should not be committed in the repository or distributed with the skill. This is not expected nor safe.
